## Response snapshot

**Treated as a stale dev-server state issue, same failure class as PHR 0031** — identical stack top frame (`runtime~main.js:843:31`), same project, same remediation. Not a code defect.

**Diagnosis.** The failing chunk is the development-mode webpack chunk for `edu-site/docs/stage-04-engineering-autonomous-ai-agents/index.md` (`content---stage-04-engineering-autonomous-ai-agents-868-151`, key `868-151` in `.docusaurus/routes.js` and `.docusaurus/registry.js`). The browser's loaded runtime referenced that chunk, but the running dev server no longer served it, so `react-loadable` surfaced a `ChunkLoadError` on client-side navigation. Chunk name generation is stable, so the current dev build produces the identical name — I confirmed the same registry key on a fresh dev-mode start.

**Contributing factors found on disk.** The `.docusaurus` state at session start had been generated at 07:42 by an earlier dev session and predates today's content churn — including the intro restructure (`docs/intro-1-binary-to-programming/01-binary.md` folder created 12:13). Separately, a full `npm run build` ran at 13:49:46-13:50:09 while the dev server was up; a build rewrites `.docusaurus` in production mode (short-hash chunk names, matching `build/assets/js/*`), which invalidates the chunk references an open dev tab holds. Running `npm run build` and `npm start` against the same folder concurrently reproduces exactly this error class.

**Remediation applied.** Stopped the test dev server, `npm run clear` (removed `.docusaurus/`, `build/`, `node_modules/.cache/`), restarted in dev mode, and verified end to end: the exact chunk URL from the error returns HTTP 200 (20,288 bytes); doc routes return 200 when requested as a browser would (`Accept: text/html`) and 404 without that header, which is the standard Docusaurus dev SPA fallback noted in PHR 0031, not a regression. Stopped the test server afterward, leaving port 3000 free.

**Verification detail worth recording.** The agent shell had `NODE_ENV=production` in its process scope (not user or machine scope), which made a first repro run compile production-style and 404 doc routes; re-running with `NODE_ENV=development` reproduced the user's real dev configuration. The user's own terminal is unaffected.

**Out of scope / untouched.** A `docusaurus serve --port 3210` (prod preview) was found running and left running; both its `/` and Stage 4 routes return 200. No source, config, theme, component, script, or dependency file was modified.

## Outcome

- ✅ Impact: Dev-server chunk state reset and verified; exact failing chunk serves 200.
- 🧪 Tests: manual HTTP checks on the chunk URL, dev routes (with/without Accept), and the 3210 prod serve.
- 📁 Files: only generated folders were cleared and regenerated; the PHR itself is the sole file authored.
- 🔁 Next prompts: user hard-refreshes the browser tab; restart `npm start` normally.
- 🧠 Reflection: ChunkLoadErrors in this project are dev-server state, not code — check the active servers before reading source.

- Failure modes observed: open browser tab holding a runtime from a previous server state; a production build clobbering `.docusaurus` under a live dev server; agent verification returning 404 when a request lacks `Accept: text/html`; `NODE_ENV=production` inherited by the agent shell tainting the first repro.
- Graders run and results (PASS/FAIL): PASS — chunk and routes serve correctly after clear + restart.
